items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the expression S = Vi t + ½at².

rubric.why: Displacement is represented by the area under the speed-time graph, which consists of a rectangle and a triangle.
rubric.description: Identifies displacement as the area under the graph and splits the area into a rectangle and a triangle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the area interpretation and division into the two shapes.

rubric.why: The rectangular area is initial speed multiplied by time.
rubric.description: Finds the rectangular area as Vi t.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct rectangular area.

rubric.why: The triangular area is ½(Vf − Vi)t, and Vf − Vi = at.
rubric.description: Finds the triangular area and uses the acceleration relation to express the velocity change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct triangular area and acceleration relation.

rubric.why: Adding the rectangular and triangular areas gives the required displacement equation.
rubric.description: Obtains the required expression for displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final expression.

modelAnswer: Displacement S equals the area under the speed-time graph.
The area consists of a rectangle and a triangle.
Since a = (Vf − Vi)/t, then Vf − Vi = at.

items.followUp: Define potential energy and derive its expression for an object at height h above Earth.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with an object's position or configuration.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy in terms of position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: Raising an object requires work against gravity.
rubric.description: Explains that work is done against gravity to raise the object.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the work done against gravity.

rubric.why: Work is force multiplied by displacement; the lifting force is mg and the vertical displacement is h.
rubric.description: Applies the work relation using gravitational force and height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using W = Fh and F = mg.

rubric.why: The work done is stored as gravitational potential energy, giving PE = mgh.
rubric.description: Derives the final expression for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final expression.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by an object because of its position or configuration.
To raise an object of mass m through height h, work is done against gravity.
The force required to lift the object is its weight, F = mg, and the displacement is h.
This work is stored as gravitational potential energy, so PE = mgh.
